name: Southern African Braai & Pot
summary: A week of Southern African home cooking: bobotie with lentils, a Cape mackerel curry, Zimbabwean beef and greens with sadza, chakalaka and beans, umngqusho and a Saturday peri-peri chicken. Maize, sorghum, beans and greens carry the week, with fatty fish on five days.
howItWorks:
**Cook once, eat twice.** Monday's bobotie, Tuesday's fish curry, Wednesday's beef and greens, Thursday's chakalaka and beans, Friday's umngqusho and Saturday's peri-peri chicken each make two portions, so the next day's lunch is already done. The mabele pot covers two breakfasts.

**Fatty fish on five days.** Pilchards on Monday, Tuesday's mackerel curry and Wednesday's leftover, pilchards on toast on Friday and Sunday's braaied mackerel give you most of the week's omega-3 and B12, and help with vitamin D. The soft pilchard bones add calcium. The braai is always cooked fresh.

**Maize, sorghum and beans.** Pap and sadza use whole-grain mealie meal, in modest portions. Whole sorghum makes the mabele, hominy stands in for samp, pinto beans for sugar beans, and lentils fill in the rest. Legumes turn up on most days.

**Greens and chicken livers.** Collards stand in for rape greens in the stew, umngqusho and braai greens, and chakalaka and fresh sambals keep every plate bright. The chicken livers on Saturday's peri-peri tray bring **iron, folate and choline**.

**Prep ahead.** Soak the sorghum on Monday night and cook the mabele on Tuesday evening while the curry simmers. Cook the chakalaka for Tuesday's eggs while Monday's bobotie bakes, and Saturday's while the umngqusho simmers. Soak the samp on Thursday night.

recipes.name: South African oats with apricots, almonds and cinnamon
recipes.inspiredBy: South African oats porridge, with dried apricots and cinnamon
recipes.about: Creamy oats cooked in milk with chopped dried apricots and a good pinch of cinnamon, topped with toasted almonds. It is warm, gently sweet and ready in about 10 minutes. The almonds bring **vitamin E and magnesium**, and the milk adds calcium and protein.
steps: Toast the almonds in a dry pan over medium heat until golden and nutty, about 3 minutes. Chop them roughly.
Put the oats, milk, apricots, cinnamon and salt in a small pot.
Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat, stirring often, until the oats are thick and creamy, about 6 minutes. Loosen with a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Spoon into a bowl and scatter the almonds over the top.
recipes.tip: Chop the apricots small so they melt into the porridge and sweeten it, with no sugar needed. Leave out the apricots and stir in a sliced ripe pear if you have no dried fruit.

recipes.name: Eggs in chakalaka with beans
recipes.inspiredBy: South African chakalaka, the spicy vegetable relish served at every braai, cooked into a breakfast skillet with beans and eggs
recipes.about: Eggs cooked until firm in a spicy tomato, pepper and carrot chakalaka with a few beans and a handful of spinach, the way South Africans love their baked beans and eggs. It is hearty, bright and a little hot. The eggs and beans bring **protein, choline and folate**.

ingredients.note: sugar beans or pinto beans, drained

steps: Warm the oil in a wide pan over medium heat. Cook the onion, green pepper and carrot until soft and starting to colour, about 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, chakalaka spice and cayenne and cook for 1 minute, until it smells toasty.
Add the tomato, beans and salt and simmer, stirring, until the tomato is jammy, about 6 minutes. Stir in the spinach until just wilted.

Make two wells in the chakalaka and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook gently until the whites and the yolks are both firm, 8 to 10 minutes. Press a yolk gently with a spoon to check that it is not runny.
Toast the bread and serve it alongside for scooping up the eggs and the sauce.
recipes.tip: Cook the chakalaka (steps 1 to 3) the evening before, while the bobotie bakes or the umngqusho simmers. Reheat it in the morning, crack in the eggs and breakfast takes about 12 minutes.

recipes.name: Mabele sorghum porridge with amasi, guava, peanuts and sunflower seeds
recipes.inspiredBy: Mabele, the sorghum porridge of Botswana, Lesotho and South Africa, eaten soft with amasi (fermented milk), made here with whole sorghum cooked soft
recipes.about: A soft, slightly nutty sorghum porridge (mabele) topped with cold, tangy amasi, ripe guava and toasted peanuts and sunflower seeds. The sorghum, peanuts and seeds bring **iron, magnesium and vitamin E**, and the amasi adds calcium and protein.

ingredients.note: plain kefir or buttermilk, for the amasi

steps: The night before, rinse the sorghum and soak it in plenty of cold water. Make enough for two mornings.

In the evening, drain the sorghum and put it in a pot with about three times as much fresh water and the salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer partly covered, stirring now and then, until the grains are tender and the porridge is thick, about 50 minutes. Top up with a splash of water if it gets dry. A pressure cooker does it in about 20 minutes.

Beat the porridge hard with a wooden spoon and mash some of the grains against the side of the pot, until it is soft and spoonable. This makes two portions, so cool both, cover and keep them in the fridge.

Next morning, toast the peanuts and sunflower seeds in a dry pan for 3 minutes. Warm one portion with a splash of water, spoon it into a bowl and pour the amasi over it. Top with the guava and the toasted nuts and seeds.
The next day, warm the second portion and top it the same way.
recipes.tip: Cook it in the evening while dinner simmers, so breakfast is only a reheat. If you cannot find amasi, kefir or buttermilk is just as tangy. Use a ripe peach or a few strawberries when guava is not in season.

recipes.name: Pilchards in tomato with soft pap and tomato and onion sambal
recipes.inspiredBy: South African pilchards and pap, the classic tinned fish lunch, with a fresh tomato and onion sambal
recipes.about: Canned pilchards warmed with onion, garlic and a handful of morogo-style greens, spooned over soft maize pap with a sharp tomato and onion sambal on the side. It is cheap, fast and a proper South African lunch. The pilchards bring **omega-3, vitamin B12 and calcium** from their soft bones.

ingredients.note: pilchards or sardines, with their tomato sauce
split between the sambal and the pan
half sliced thin for the sambal

steps: Make the sambal first so the flavours meet. Slice half the onion very thin and chop half the tomato. Toss them with the lemon juice, a pinch of cayenne, a pinch of salt and the cilantro, and leave it to sit.

Bring a pot of water to a boil, about five times the weight of the meal for a soft, spoonable pap, with a pinch of salt. Whisk in the cornmeal in a slow stream so there are no lumps. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook, stirring often, until the pap is thick and soft, about 15 minutes.
While the pap cooks, warm the oil in a small pan. Cook the rest of the onion and the garlic until soft, about 4 minutes. Add the remaining tomato and cook until saucy, about 3 minutes.
Tip in the pilchards with their sauce and break them up gently. Add the spinach and warm everything through until the spinach has just wilted, about 3 minutes.
Spoon the pap onto a plate, top with the pilchards and serve the sambal alongside.
recipes.tip: Use plain white cornmeal (whole-grain if you can find it), not masa harina or precooked arepa flour. Sardines in tomato sauce work if you cannot find pilchards.

recipes.name: Bobotie-inspired lentil and beef bake with turmeric rice and carrot sambal
recipes.inspiredBy: Cape Malay bobotie, spiced mince baked under an egg custard, with lentils sharing the work and brown rice for the usual yellow rice
recipes.about: Gently spiced beef and lentils with apricots and chutney, baked under a golden egg and milk custard, with turmeric brown rice and a bright carrot sambal. It is sweet, savoury and comforting, and it is even better the next day. The beef and lentils together bring **iron, zinc and plenty of protein**.
steps: Heat the oven to 180C (350F). Rinse the rice and put it in a pot with plenty of water and half the turmeric. Simmer, covered, until tender, about 35 minutes, then drain. Make enough for two portions.
At the same time, simmer the lentils in plenty of water until just tender, about 25 minutes, and drain.
Warm the oil in a large pan. Cook the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, Cape Malay masala, cinnamon and the rest of the turmeric and cook for 1 minute, until fragrant.
Add the beef and break it up as it browns, about 6 minutes. Stir in the lentils, chutney, apricots, half the lemon juice, salt and a splash of water. Simmer for 5 minutes, until moist but not wet.

Press the mixture into a baking dish and tuck the bay leaves on top. Beat the eggs with the milk and a pinch of salt and pour this over. Bake until the custard is set and lightly golden, about 25 minutes.
While it bakes, toss the grated carrot with the remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt for the sambal.
Serve a portion of bobotie with the rice and the carrot sambal. This makes two portions, so pack the second for tomorrow's lunch. It reheats well, or eat it cold.
recipes.tip: Use lean ground lamb if you like, which is also very Cape. For extra tang, serve a spoonful of chutney on the side.

recipes.name: Cape Malay-style mackerel and butternut curry with spinach
recipes.inspiredBy: Cape Malay fish curry, with tamarind for the sour note and butternut for sweetness
recipes.about: Chunks of mackerel simmered gently in a tomato and tamarind curry with sweet butternut and spinach, finished with lemon and cilantro. It is fragrant rather than fiery, with the sweet and sour balance the Cape does so well. The butternut adds **vitamin A**, and mackerel is a rich source of **omega-3, vitamin B12 and vitamin D**.

ingredients.note: fillets with skin, cut in chunks

steps: Peel the butternut and cut it into 2 cm chunks. Cut the mackerel into big chunks, leaving the skin on, and sprinkle with half the salt and a little of the turmeric.
Warm the oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, Cape Malay masala and the rest of the turmeric. Stir for 1 minute until it smells wonderful.
Add the tomato, tamarind, chutney and a mug of water, then add the butternut. Cover and simmer until it is nearly tender, about 12 minutes.

Nestle the mackerel into the sauce, cover and cook gently until it flakes, 6 to 8 minutes. Do not stir hard or the fish will break up. Fold in the spinach for the last 2 minutes, just until it wilts, then add the lemon juice, cilantro and the rest of the salt.
This makes two portions. Pack the second for tomorrow's lunch and reheat it gently.
recipes.tip: Serve with rice or a roti for a bigger plate. Any oily fish works, such as sardines or fresh snoek if you have it.

recipes.name: Zimbabwean beef stew with peanut greens and sadza
recipes.inspiredBy: Zimbabwean sadza ne nyama with muriwo une dovi, greens cooked in ground peanuts (a peanut butter sauce)
recipes.about: Slow-simmered beef in a tomato and onion gravy, with collard greens cooked in crushed roasted peanuts, and a modest portion of sadza to scoop it all up. It is the everyday Zimbabwean plate, and the greens make it so much more than meat and starch. Beef and greens together bring **iron, zinc and B12**, and the collards add calcium.

ingredients.note: like Zimbabwean rape greens, ribs removed and sliced thin
whole-grain white mealie meal, for the sadza

steps: Warm half the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the beef in batches until deeply browned, about 8 minutes, and set aside.
In the same pot, cook two thirds of the onion until soft. Add the garlic, black pepper, bay leaves and cayenne, then the tomato, and cook until it breaks down into a sauce, about 6 minutes.

Return the beef to the pot with enough water to just cover it. Cover and simmer very gently until the beef is tender and the gravy is thick, about 90 minutes, or 35 minutes in a pressure cooker. Season with the salt near the end. This makes two portions.

For the greens, soften the rest of the onion in the remaining oil in a wide pan. Add the collards with a splash of water and cook, covered, for 6 minutes, then add the spinach and cook until both are silky and tender, about 4 more minutes. Stir in the crushed peanuts and a spoonful of the stew gravy and cook for 2 more minutes, until glossy and not wet.

For the sadza, bring water to a boil, about three times the weight of the meal. Stir a third of the meal with a splash of cold water to a slurry, whisk it into the boiling water and simmer for 5 minutes. Add the rest in handfuls, beating hard with a wooden spoon, then cover and cook on low for 5 minutes. Beat again until stiff and smooth.
Serve the sadza with the beef and the greens. Pack the second portion of stew and greens for tomorrow's lunch, and make a fresh small pot of sadza then, or reheat the leftover with a splash of water.
recipes.tip: A pressure cooker makes this a weeknight dish: 35 minutes for the beef. A spoonful of smooth peanut butter can stand in for the crushed peanuts. Collards stand in for the rape greens (kale-like) Zimbabweans use. Kale or chard work too, and amaranth leaves (morogo) are the traditional choice if you can find them.

recipes.name: Chakalaka and beans with boerewors-style beef patties and sweet potato
recipes.inspiredBy: South African chakalaka and beans, with lean beef patties seasoned like boerewors (coriander, clove and nutmeg) instead of the fatty sausage
recipes.about: A thick, spicy vegetable and bean stew, chakalaka, with juicy herb-and-spice beef patties seasoned like boerewors, and roasted sweet potato wedges to catch the sauce. It is the comfort food of any South African table. The beans and vegetables bring **fibre, folate and vitamin C**, and the sweet potato adds vitamin A.

ingredients.note: 30 g grated for the patties, the rest diced
chopped, or use a can of crushed
pinto beans in place of sugar beans, drained

steps: Cut the sweet potato into wedges and roast on a tray at 220C (425F) until soft and browned at the edges, about 25 minutes, turning once.
Mix the beef with the grated onion, boerewors spice, lemon juice and half the salt. The grated onion keeps lean beef juicy. Shape into patties and let them rest for 10 minutes.
Warm the oil in a wide pan. Cook the diced onion, green pepper and carrot until soft, about 8 minutes. Add the garlic, chakalaka spice and cayenne and cook for 1 minute.
Add the tomato and simmer until thick, about 10 minutes. Stir in the beans and the rest of the salt and cook until the chakalaka is thick and jammy, about 8 minutes.

Pan-fry the patties in a non-stick pan over medium heat, using a little of the oil, until well browned and cooked through to 71 C (160 F) inside, about 4 minutes per side. Wash your hands and the board after handling the raw beef.
Stir the cilantro into the chakalaka. Serve the patties on the beans with the sweet potato wedges alongside.
This makes two portions. Pack the second for tomorrow's lunch. The patties are good cold or reheated in a pan.
recipes.tip: Ask for a lean grind, 95% lean, so the patties stay light. Lean ground lamb or turkey also work. Cook the chakalaka a day ahead: it only improves.

recipes.name: Umngqusho, samp and beans with lamb and greens
recipes.inspiredBy: Xhosa umngqusho, the slow-cooked samp and sugar bean dish, with a little lamb for flavour and greens folded in
recipes.about: Sugar beans and a little samp (dried hominy) simmered with lamb, onion, garlic and a little butter, finished with tomato, collard greens and cilantro. It is slow, filling food from the Eastern Cape. Beans and samp together bring **fibre, iron and folate**, the collards add calcium and the lamb adds zinc and B12.

ingredients.note: dried hominy, in place of samp, soaked overnight
pinto beans in place of sugar beans, canned, drained

steps: The night before, soak the samp in plenty of cold water. Drain it in the morning.

Melt the butter with the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat. Brown the lamb for about 6 minutes, then add the onion and cook until soft, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, bay leaves, black pepper and cayenne.

Add the drained samp and enough water to cover by two finger widths. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer gently, stirring now and then and topping up the water, until the samp is very tender and creamy, about 2 hours, or 45 minutes in a pressure cooker.
With 30 minutes left, stir in the beans and tomato and cook uncovered, mashing a few beans against the side of the pot so they melt into the samp.
Fold in the collards and cook for 8 minutes, until silky and tender. Stir in the cilantro and the salt.
This makes two portions. Pack the second for tomorrow's lunch. The pot keeps 4 days in the fridge, and freezes well.
recipes.tip: Real samp and sugar beans from a South African shop swap in by weight. Borlotti is the closest canned bean. Canned hominy, rinsed, also works: add it with the beans and the pot is ready in 40 minutes. Short on time? A pressure cooker makes dried samp a weeknight option.

recipes.name: Peri-peri chicken and livers with roasted butternut and spinach salad
recipes.inspiredBy: Mozambican and Portuguese frango piri-piri, with the roasted butternut salad you find at a South African braai
recipes.about: Chicken thighs and livers marinated in peri-peri, lemon and garlic and roasted until sticky and browned, with sweet roasted butternut, spinach, sliced onion and toasted pumpkin seeds. It is bold, smoky and bright, cooled with a lemony amasi drizzle, and the leftovers make a good cold plate tomorrow. The livers bring **iron, folate and choline**, the butternut and spinach add vitamin A and K, and the pumpkin seeds add zinc.

ingredients.note: sliced thin, red if you have it
plain kefir or buttermilk, for the drizzle

steps: Stir together the peri-peri sauce, half the lemon juice, the garlic, smoked paprika, half the oil and half the salt. Rub it all over the chicken thighs, and toss the trimmed livers in a spoonful of it too. Marinate the thighs for at least 30 minutes, or overnight, and keep the livers in the fridge until you need them.
Heat the oven to 220C (425F). Toss the butternut with the rest of the oil and salt on one tray. Put the chicken on another tray.

Roast the butternut until golden at the edges, about 30 minutes, turning once. Roast the chicken until it is browned and sticky at the edges and the juices run clear, 25 to 30 minutes, adding the livers to the tray for the last 8 minutes, until browned outside and just cooked through.
Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes.

Toss the sliced onion with a squeeze of the lemon juice and a pinch of salt and leave it for 5 minutes to soften. Stir the rest of the lemon juice into the kefir with the cilantro to make a cooling amasi drizzle.
Pile the spinach on a plate, top with the warm butternut, the onion and the seeds. Serve the chicken and livers alongside, spoon the pan juices over them and drizzle with the amasi.
This makes two portions. Pack the second for tomorrow's lunch, with the spinach, seeds and amasi drizzle kept separate until you eat.
recipes.tip: Livers go grainy when reheated, so eat the leftover livers cold, sliced over the salad. Not a liver fan? Leave them out and add a little more chicken. Marinate overnight for the best flavour. Serve extra peri-peri at the table for people who like it hot, and use a mild sauce for kids.

recipes.name: Braaied mackerel with chutney glaze, sweet potato, greens and bean salad
recipes.inspiredBy: South African braaied snoek, basted with sweet chutney, butter and lemon, with mackerel standing in for snoek
recipes.about: Mackerel fillets brushed with a sticky chutney, lemon and garlic glaze and grilled hot, with sweet potatoes baked in foil, garlicky greens and a tangy bean and tomato salad. It is a Sunday braai at its best, and works on a grill or under the broiler. Mackerel gives you a big dose of **omega-3, vitamin D and B12**.

ingredients.note: a spoonful for the glaze, the rest for the salad and fish
minced, half for the glaze and half for the greens
pinto beans in place of sugar beans, drained

steps: Heat the grill (braai or broiler) until very hot. Wrap the sweet potatoes in foil with a pinch of salt and cook on the coals or at 200C (400F) until tender, about 40 minutes. A few minutes in the microwave first speeds it up.
Warm the butter, chutney, a spoonful of the lemon juice, half the garlic and the cayenne in a small pan until melted and runny, about 2 minutes.
Toss the beans, tomato, onion, oil, cilantro and half the lemon juice with a pinch of salt and let the salad sit while the fish cooks.
Warm a little of the oil in a pan and cook the collards with the rest of the garlic and a splash of water, covered, until silky and tender, about 8 minutes. Keep warm.

Pat the mackerel dry and season it with salt and pepper. Brush it with the glaze. Grill skin side down on a lightly oiled grid for about 4 minutes, brush again, then flip and cook 2 to 3 minutes more, until it flakes. Under a broiler, cook skin side up for 6 to 7 minutes and skip the flip.
Squeeze the rest of the lemon juice over the fish and serve it with the sweet potatoes, the garlicky collards and the bean salad.
recipes.tip: Fresh snoek is the real thing if you can get it. Mackerel is richer and easier to find. Cook it fresh on the day, not as a leftover.

recipes.name: Guava with roasted peanuts
recipes.about: Sweet and slightly tart guava with a handful of roasted peanuts, the kind of snack you would grab from a South African fruit stall. Guava has more **vitamin C** than an orange, and the peanuts add protein and vitamin E.
steps: Cut the guava into wedges. The seeds are soft, so you can eat them.
Eat with the peanuts, in alternating bites.

recipes.name: Biltong with almonds
recipes.inspiredBy: South African biltong, the air-dried spiced beef eaten at every braai
recipes.about: Thin strips of dried, spiced beef with a handful of almonds, a salty and crunchy pairing. Biltong packs a lot of **protein and iron** into a small snack, and the almonds add vitamin E.
steps: Slice the biltong into thin strips if it is in a piece.
Eat a strip of biltong with a few almonds, or just alternate bites.
recipes.tip: Buy biltong at a South African shop or online. For jerky, pick the plainest, least sweet one, never teriyaki.

recipes.name: Amasi with mango
recipes.about: Cold, thick amasi (fermented milk) with sweet ripe mango. It brings **calcium and protein**, with vitamin A and vitamin C from the mango.

ingredients.note: plain kefir or buttermilk, for the amasi

steps: Spoon the kefir into a bowl.
Top with the diced mango and eat it cold.

recipes.name: Amasi with guava
recipes.about: Cold, tangy amasi (fermented milk) with soft, fragrant guava. It brings **calcium and protein**, and the guava adds more vitamin C than an orange.

ingredients.note: plain kefir or buttermilk, for the amasi

steps: Spoon the kefir into a bowl.
Top with the diced guava and eat it cold.

recipes.name: Dried apricots with almonds
recipes.about: Chewy Cape-style dried apricots with a handful of almonds, a snack that keeps in the bag all day. The apricots bring vitamin A and potassium, and the almonds add **vitamin E and magnesium**.
steps: Put the apricots and almonds in a small bowl.
Eat them together so the sweet apricot balances the crunch.

recipes.name: Mielie with butter, lemon and chili
recipes.about: A braaied or boiled cob of sweet corn with a little butter, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of chili, the way it is sold at roadside stalls. Roadside mielies are starchier; sweet corn is the closest cob here. It is a **whole-food starch** with fibre and folate.

ingredients.note: kernels cut from one large cob

steps: Bring a pot of salted water to a boil, or heat a grill until hot.
Boil the cob until the kernels are tender, about 8 minutes, or grill it, turning often, until it is charred in spots, about 12 minutes.
Rub the hot cob with the butter, squeeze over the lemon and finish with a pinch of cayenne.

recipes.name: Mango with lemon and chili
recipes.about: Ripe mango strips with a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of chili, a bright, sweet and spicy street-stall snack. It brings **vitamin C and vitamin A**.
steps: Cut the mango into strips.
Squeeze the lemon over it and dust with a pinch of cayenne.

recipes.name: Pilchards on toast with tomato
recipes.inspiredBy: South African pilchards on toast, a classic tinned-fish snack
recipes.about: Tinned pilchards mashed onto warm whole-wheat toast with sliced tomato, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of chili, an old South African favourite. It is a quick hit of **omega-3, calcium and vitamin B12**, since the soft bones are edible.

ingredients.note: pilchards or sardines, with their sauce

steps: Toast the bread until golden and crisp.
Mash the pilchards lightly with a fork, bones and all, then spread them over the toast.
Top with the tomato, a squeeze of lemon and a pinch of cayenne.
recipes.tip: The rest of the tin keeps 2 days, covered, in the fridge.

recipes.name: Peri-peri pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Pumpkin seeds toasted with smoked paprika, cayenne and a squeeze of lemon, a crunchy bag-of-the-day snack. They are one of the best food sources of **magnesium and zinc**.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan over medium heat, stirring, until they puff and pop, about 4 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the smoked paprika, cayenne, salt and lemon juice. It sizzles and coats the seeds. Cool a minute before eating.

recipes.name: Dried apricots with toasted pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Chewy dried apricots with a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds, a sweet and crunchy bag-of-the-day snack. The apricots bring vitamin A and potassium, and the seeds add **zinc and magnesium**.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes.
Eat them with the apricots, a few of each in every bite.

recipes.name: Mango with dried apricots
recipes.about: Fresh ripe mango with a few chewy dried apricots, a double dose of sweet and tangy fruit. It brings **vitamin A and vitamin C** and a good amount of potassium.
steps: Dice the mango into a bowl.
Chop the apricots small and scatter them over the mango.

recipes.name: Mango with toasted pumpkin seeds
recipes.about: Ripe mango with a handful of toasted pumpkin seeds, sweet and nutty. The mango brings **vitamin C and vitamin A**, and the seeds add zinc and magnesium.
steps: Toast the pumpkin seeds in a dry pan until they pop, about 3 minutes.
Dice the mango and scatter the seeds over it.
